transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I've been having a lot of trouble organizing my thoughts and expressing what I mean lately. I also feel very unmotivated to do anything, and this all started about four months ago.
Have you struggled with these difficulties in focus and motivation your entire life, or were you functioning well before these symptoms began four months ago?

I started noticing some smaller changes and struggles about a year and ten months ago. But it wasn't nearly this bad back then. The really severe lack of motivation and focus only became a major problem about four months ago.

During those past 22 months, have you experienced any periods lasting longer than two months where you felt completely back to your normal self, or has there been some level of these symptoms present for most of that time?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. I don't think I've had any periods where I felt completely back to my normal self, as there has always been some level of this cloudiness there.

Since your symptoms have been present for 22 months without a two-month break, have you experienced a period within these last four months where your symptoms were severe enough to meet the full criteria for a major depressive episode?
I'm not really sure about that. I don't know what a major depressive episode actually entails, so I can't say if my symptoms fit that description.

To help clarify, have you experienced a persistent low mood or a loss of interest in almost all activities, along with physical symptoms like changes in your sleep, appetite, or energy levels, for most of the day nearly every day over these past four months?

I have definitely lost interest in almost all the activities I used to enjoy, and I just can't find the motivation to start anything lately. However, I haven't really noticed a low mood, and my sleep, appetite, and energy levels haven't changed much.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a chronic, persistent state of low motivation and cognitive cloudiness lasting for 22 months without a two-month symptom-free interval. Although the patient does not report a distinct major depressive episode, the chronic nature of the symptoms meets the duration and character criteria for Persistent Depressive Disorder.
